vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 1.0.17

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle for CellCog appears benign. It provides instructions and code snippets for integrating with the CellCog AI service, including API key management, task creation, and file processing. All network communication is directed to the legitimate `cellcog.ai` domain, and file access examples use generic paths (`/data/`). There is no evidence of intentional malicious behavior such as unauthorized data exfiltration, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection designed to subvert the agent for harmful purposes. The instructions are transparent about the skill's capabilities and interactions.

llm.summary: The skill generally matches its stated purpose (an SDK-backed Any-to-Any AI) but contains inconsistencies in its declared metadata vs runtime instructions and instructs the agent to include arbitrary local files in requests—behaviors that merit caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes an SDK-based service (CellCog) and asks for an API key and pip install of a 'cellcog' package—these are coherent with the described capability. However the registry metadata provided earlier claimed no required env vars and no install spec while the SKILL.md frontmatter declares env: [CELLCOG_API_KEY] and install: pip: cellcog. This mismatch is unexpected and should be clarified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly show embedding absolute local file paths inside <SHOW_FILE> tags so the agent will read and send arbitrary local files (PDFs, spreadsheets, audio, images) to the external CellCog service. That is consistent with the skill's purpose but represents a real exfiltration risk if the agent is allowed to include sensitive files (passwords, keys, private repos, etc.). The SKILL.md also gives examples of delivering many outputs and notifying 'agent:main:main' which could cause automated delivery of results—verify where those outputs go.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md requests pip install cellcog (PyPI) and lists python3 in bins. Installing a third-party PyPI package is a normal install route for an SDK, but this is higher-risk than instruction-only skills because it writes code to disk. The registry entry elsewhere said 'No install spec'—another inconsistency to resolve. You should confirm the package origin (official PyPI project, maintainer, source repository) before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions require a single API credential (CELLCOG_API_KEY), which is proportionate to an external SDK. However the registry metadata at the top claimed 'Required env vars: none' and 'Primary credential: none'—this contradiction is suspicious. Also an API key grants the remote service ability to receive whatever files you send; confirm what the API key scope, billing/credit implications, and data retention policies are.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not ask to modify other skills or system-wide settings. It appears to rely on the agent invoking the SDK at runtime; no elevated platform privileges are requested by the skill manifest.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: 1) Clarify the metadata mismatch (registry says no env/install but SKILL.md requests CELLCOG_API_KEY and pip install). 2) Verify the 'cellcog' pip package origin and inspect its source on PyPI/GitHub; avoid installing unknown packages into production environments. 3) Treat the <SHOW_FILE> mechanism as capable of exfiltrating any local file—do not allow the agent to access sensitive directories or secrets when using this skill. 4) Limit the API key's scope and billing exposure (use a test account or scoped key, and monitor credits). 5) Review CellCog's privacy/data-retention policy and confirm whether data sent will be stored or used to train models. 6) If you must test, do so with non-sensitive sample files and in an isolated environment. If these questions cannot be answered or the package/project cannot be verified, do not install or provide real credentials.
